a.side: lane genres on origin/main, before P55

pick: pure-rand xoroshiro128plus(55006): uniformInt without replacement per genre in turn (catch, whack, slice, defense) over P54C dev targets

pairs.text: catch the falling apples but dodge the rotten ones
pairs.why: Game B has more simultaneous falling rewards and bombs, with threats approaching the player and busier action in the later scenes. Game A stays comparatively sparse, with longer gaps between objects and less buildup toward the end.

pairs.text: catch raindrops in a cup but not the lightning bolts
pairs.why: Game B has busier early waves, with clusters of blue drops, yellow pickups, and bombs descending toward the player, while Game A mostly shows isolated objects and longer quiet stretches. Both become similarly sparse near the end without much buildup, but B offers more action and danger overall.

pairs.text: place cannons to hold the lanes against invading crabs on the beach
pairs.why: Game A shows more activity, with glowing shots and a ring appearing along the lanes, including several effects near the end. Game B mostly shows the turtle changing position beneath an otherwise similar scene, with little visible buildup or danger close to the player.

pairs.text: a ninja slices fruit tossed in the air but avoids the bombs
pairs.why: Game A builds toward a busier finish, with a glowing ring, several yellow objects near the platforms, and a dark projectile overhead. Game B shows similar early action but fewer objects late on, while A’s player also moves between lanes more often.

pairs.text: smash the aliens that pop out of craters on the moon
pairs.why: Game A has more sustained activity, with glowing ringed blue figures remaining visible alongside the orange creatures, while Game B has more empty holes between appearances. A also ends with the robot close to the orange creature on the right, giving the final scene more immediate danger than B.

pairs.text: a hammer game where goblins peek out of barrels and you whack them
pairs.why: Game B builds up with emerging creatures and a highlighted green object close to the player in the later scenes, giving it more nearby action. Game A shows movement and occasional creatures too, but ends with empty holes and less visible activity.
